text.tspan: Make the tag the rule, not the exception.
Incentives work better than
mandates: let paying in cash cost more and take more time, as it
already does in Santiago and Montevideo - Uruguay charges 22% less
with TAG and Chile announced discounts of 10% to 25% on Autopista
Central.
Let cash pay its real cost.
Every cash stop costs time for everyone
behind. The surcharge for late or manual payment is not a punishment:
it is the price of the friction it creates.
At gas stations, safety before habit.
The Uruguay case is measured:
25% fewer robberies. The debate is not whether cash is cheaper, but
for whom and at what cost. And the cost is paid by workers on the
night shift.
Parking: one way to pay, or none.
As long as every city and every
operator has its own app, cash will remain the plan B. Interoperability -
the same tag working for the toll and the parking lot - is what turned the
tag into the rule in Chile. That is the model.
